explanation: The basal ganglia are supplied by central branches of anterior & middle cerebral arteries. Its anterior parts are supplied by anterior cerebral artery & their posterior parts are supplied by middle cerebral artery.

subject: Anatomy
text: Which cranial nerve nuclei are located in the pons?
explanation: The trigeminal and abducent nuclei are situated within the pons. Oculomotor lies in the midbrain and hypoglossal/vagus in the medulla.
keyConcept: The pons houses the trigeminal and abducent nuclei.

subject: Anatomy
text: Which structure end in the internal jugular vein?
explanation: The inferior petrosal sinus ends in the internal jugular vein at the base of the skull. It drains the cavernous sinus posteriorly.
keyConcept: The inferior petrosal sinus terminates in the internal jugular vein.

subject: Anatomy
text: Which of the following cranial nerves passes through the cavernous sinus?
explanation: The abducent nerve runs through the cavernous sinus near the internal carotid artery. The other ocular motor nerves travel in the lateral wall.
keyConcept: The abducent nerve traverses the cavernous sinus.

subject: Anatomy
text: The Superior Cerebral Veins primarily drain into which of the following dural venous sinuses?
explanation: After draining into the transverse and then sigmoid sinus, cerebral venous blood ultimately passes through the sigmoid sinus toward the jugular vein. In this item the sigmoid sinus is the selected route.
keyConcept: Cerebral venous blood passes through the sigmoid sinus toward the jugular vein.

subject: Anatomy
text: Which of the following venous sinuses drains directly into the internal jugular vein (IJV)?
explanation: The inferior petrosal sinus drains directly into the internal jugular vein. It connects the cavernous sinus to the jugular system.
keyConcept: The inferior petrosal sinus opens into the internal jugular vein.

subject: Anatomy
text: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is primarily drained into the venous system by which of the following structures?
explanation: Arachnoid granulations transfer CSF into the dural venous sinuses, chiefly the superior sagittal sinus. They are the principal site of CSF reabsorption.
keyConcept: Arachnoid granulations return CSF to the venous system.

subject: Anatomy
text: Which of the following structures is responsible for draining cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) into the venous system?
explanation: Arachnoid villi project into the venous sinuses and drain CSF into the bloodstream. They function as pressure-dependent one-way valves.
keyConcept: Arachnoid villi drain CSF into the dural venous sinuses.

subject: Anatomy
text: Which of the following arteries is connected to the posterior cerebral artery (PCA) by posterior communicating artery?
explanation: The posterior communicating artery connects the internal carotid artery to the posterior cerebral artery. This completes the posterior circle of Willis.
keyConcept: The posterior communicating artery links the internal carotid and posterior cerebral arteries.

subject: Anatomy
text: Which of the following structures receives its sensory innervation from the trigeminal nerve?

explanation: The upper eyelid receives trigeminal (ophthalmic division) sensory innervation. The other regions are supplied by cervical or glossopharyngeal nerves.
keyConcept: The trigeminal nerve innervates the upper eyelid.

subject: Physiology
text: Which of the following is true regarding the representation in the somatosensory area one S1?
options: Receive ipsilateral solitario-thalamo-cortical fibers from thalamus
Face sensation is represented posteriorly, and body sensation is represented anteriorly
Face sensation is represented anteriorly, and body sensation is represented posteriorly
Face and body sensation is represented contralaterally
explanation: The primary somatosensory area (S1) represents the face and body of the contralateral side. Representation is also disproportionate, but contralateral organization is the correct statement here.
keyConcept: S1 represents the contralateral face and body.

subject: Physiology
text: Contralateral representation of face and body is founded in ……
explanation: Contralateral representation of the face and body is found in the primary somatosensory area. Each hemisphere processes sensation from the opposite body half.
keyConcept: The primary somatosensory area holds contralateral face and body representation.

subject: Physiology
text: Which of the following pairs is matched correctly in the motor hierarchy?
options: Areas 5 and 7 –awareness of body position in space
explanation: Parietal areas 5 and 7 provide awareness of body position in space. Area 4 executes movement and areas 3, 1, 2 process sensation.
keyConcept: Areas 5 and 7 give awareness of body position in space.

subject: Physiology
text: A patient presents with hypertonia, exaggerated reflexes, and signs of an upper motor neuron lesion. Which mechanism best explains these findings?
explanation: Upper motor neuron hypertonia and hyperreflexia arise from unopposed pontine reticulospinal facilitation of extensor tone. Cortical inhibition of this pathway is lost.
keyConcept: Unopposed pontine reticulospinal drive produces UMN hypertonia.

subject: Biochemistry
lecture: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism
text: A mother notices that her month-old baby’s urine has a sweet, burnt sugar smell while changing the diaper. Laboratory tests reveal elevated levels of leucine, isoleucine, and valine in the blood. Which enzyme deficiency is most likely responsible for this condition?
explanation: The infant has maple syrup urine disease from deficiency of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex. Branched-chain amino acids and their ketoacids accumulate.
keyConcept: Branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase deficiency underlies maple syrup urine disease.
